question.worked_solution:
We use the cosecant-cotangent identity:

$$
1+{cot}^{2}⁡x={csc}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using the above, we compute the given integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /4}^{\pi /2}(1+{cot}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\pi /4}^{\pi /2}{csc}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\operatorname{cot}⁡x\,{|}_{\pi /4}^{\pi /2} \\  & =-\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-(-\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})) \\  & =-0-(-1) \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$
